The Committee comprises a Chair and up to ten (10) members, appointed by the Minister. Membership is drawn from consumer advocacy, industry, manufacturing, retail, standards development, and relevant academic or technical fields. The Chair and members are appointed for terms of up to three (3) years and may be reappointed.

**4.2 Founding Members and Biographies (as at establishment, March 2019)**

The following individuals were appointed as founding members of the Committee:

| Name | Role | Background |
|------|------|------------|
| Mr. Robert Hargreaves | Chair (inaugural) | Former Deputy Secretary, Department of Fair Trading NSW; extensive experience in consumer protection policy and product safety regulation. |
| Dr. Margaret Chen | Member | Senior Lecturer in Materials Engineering, University of Melbourne; specialist in polymer degradation and product failure analysis. |
| Ms. Anita Prasad | Member | Chief Executive, Australian Consumer Advocacy Network; long-standing campaigner for product safety standards for household appliances. |
| Mr. David Okafor | Member | Group Quality Assurance Director, HomeStyle Appliances Pty Ltd; expertise in manufacturing quality systems and supply chain auditing. |
| Ms. Helen T. Wu | Member | Principal Consultant, Standards & Compliance Partners; former manager at Standards Australia, involved in development of AS/NZS electrical safety standards. |
| Mr. James Whitfield | Member | National Secretary, Retailers and Distributors Association of Australia; background in retail logistics and product recall coordination. |
| Prof. Alan R. Stewart | Member | Professor of Consumer Law, University of Sydney; research focus on product liability and consumer redress mechanisms. |
| Ms. Grace Liu | Member | Product Safety Officer, CHOICE (consumer organisation); experience in comparative product testing and public information campaigns. |

**4.3 Appointment of Chair (2021)**

On 1 July 2021, Dr. Margaret Chen was appointed Chair of the Committee, succeeding Mr. Robert Hargreaves whose term concluded on 30 June 2021. Dr. Chen’s appointment as Chair took effect from that date, and she continues to serve in that capacity.

**5. OPERATING ARRANGEMENTS**

**5.1 Meetings**

The Committee shall meet at least four (4) times per calendar year, or more frequently as required by the Minister or the Chair. Meetings may be held in person or by electronic means. The first meeting of the Committee is scheduled for 12 April 2019 at the Department’s offices in Canberra.

**5.2 Quorum**

A quorum of half the current membership, including the Chair (or Deputy Chair if appointed), is required for a meeting to proceed. Decisions are made by consensus where possible; where consensus cannot be reached, matters may be put to a vote, with a simple majority of members present required for a recommendation to be adopted.

**5.3 Subcommittees**

National Consumer Product Quality Committee established_date 2019-03-14 date. Record status: current.

The Committee may establish subcommittees or working groups to consider specific matters, subject to the approval of the Chair. Subcommittees report to the full Committee.

**5.4 Secretariat**

The Department of Industry, Science and Resources provides secretariat support to the Committee. The Secretariat is responsible for arranging meetings, preparing agendas and minutes, and managing correspondence.

**5.5 Reporting**

The Committee reports to the Minister through the Chair. Annual reports and any other formal advice are provided in writing to the Minister.

**6. CONDUCT AND CONFLICT OF INTEREST**

Members are expected to act in the public interest, maintain confidentiality where required, and declare any conflicts of interest at the commencement of each meeting or when a relevant matter arises. Declared conflicts are recorded in the minutes of the meeting.

**7. REVIEW AND TERMINATION**

This Charter will be reviewed within three (3) years of establishment. The Minister may amend the Charter or dissolve the Committee at any time, following consultation with the Chair where practicable.

4. DECLARATIONS OF INTEREST
Members were reminded of their obligation to declare any conflicts. He stated he would withdraw from any vote on the matter if required. The Chair noted the declaration; no objection was raised.

5. REPORTS FROM WORKING GROUPS
5.1 Working Group on Portable Electric Heaters (WG-2023/04) – Verbal update by Ms. Nguyen (Chair of WG).
Ms. Nguyen reported that the WG had completed its review of test data and incident reports for three models, including the X-1000. A full report was circulated to members prior to the meeting (Attachment 1 – not included in this record). The WG recommended that the Committee consider the safety rating for the X-1000 as a matter of urgency, given the volume of incident reports.

6. NEW BUSINESS – SAFETY RATING OF THE MODEL X-1000 PORTABLE HEATER
[Note: The Chair advised that this item was the subject of a formal motion, to be considered in accordance with the Committee’s procedures for consumer product safety assessments.]

The Model X-1000 Portable Heater has a safety_rating of Unsafe, as decided by the committee. Record status: current.

6.1 Summary of evidence presented:
Ms. Nguyen presented a summary of the test results and incident data for the Model X-1000 Portable Heater (hereafter “the heater”). Key points raised during discussion:
- The heater, manufactured in China and imported by Aussie Home Comforts Pty Ltd, has been on the Australian market since July 2023.
- Testing conducted at an NATA-accredited laboratory (report ref. T-2024-0117) found that the heater’s power cord insulation did not meet the relevant Australian Standard (AS/NZS 60335.2.30) under thermal stress conditions. The test report noted “visible deformation of the cord sheath at temperatures consistent with normal use in a confined space.”
- The heater also failed a drop test, with the rear grille detaching on impact.
- Incident reports: The Committee had before it 14 incident reports received between August 2023 and February 2024, including three reports of minor property damage (scorched carpet, melted cord) and one report of a consumer receiving a mild electric shock (no medical treatment required).
- Mr. Reece, while not formally withdrawing from the discussion, stated that the importer had advised him that they believed the failures were due to “batch-specific issues” and that they had already implemented changes to the production line. He did not provide documentary evidence to the Committee.
- Ms. Nguyen noted that the importer had not yet provided a formal written submission despite being invited to do so on two occasions (letters dated 15 Jan and 5 Feb 2024).
- The Chair noted that the product’s safety_rating of Unsafe is a category rating, as defined in the Committee’s Operating Procedures (Section 4.2). This rating is current and remains in effect until the Committee determines otherwise.
- Dr. Tran (Chair) also noted that a recall recommendation, if passed, would be referred to the ACCC for action.

6.2 Motion:
Moved by Ms. Carla Nguyen: “That the Committee recommends that the Model X-1000 Portable Heater be recalled, and that the safety_rating of the Model X-1000 Portable Heater be recorded as Unsafe, as decided by the committee.”
Seconded by Ms. Fiona Gallagher (Consumer Representative, SA).

6.3 Discussion on the motion:
- Ms. Gallagher noted that the number of incidents, while not high, was significant given the product had only been on the market for eight months. She expressed concern that the heater was sold through major retailers and was likely to be used in bedrooms and other small spaces.
- Mr. Reece asked whether the Committee had considered the importer’s corrective actions. Ms. Nguyen confirmed that the WG had requested evidence of the corrective actions on 12 Feb 2024, but no response had been received as of the meeting date.
- The Chair reminded members that the Committee’s role is to make a recommendation based on available evidence, and that the importer would have the opportunity to make a submission to the ACCC during any recall process.
The minutes of the meeting held on 6 February 2024 were confirmed as a true and accurate record. Moved by Ms. Gallagher, seconded by Mr. Okafor. Carried unanimously.

Apologies were noted. Mr. Reece declared an interest in agenda item 6 (Model X-1000 Portable Heater) on the basis that his employer has a commercial relationship with the importer, but stated he would participate in the discussion unless the Committee requested otherwise. No objection was raised.

documents.content:
The Committee comprises a Chair and up to ten (10) members, appointed by the Minister. Membership is drawn from consumer advocacy, industry, manufacturing, retail, standards development, and relevant academic or technical fields. The Chair and members are appointed for terms of up to three (3) years and may be reappointed.

**4.2 Founding Members and Biographies (as at establishment, March 2019)**

The following individuals were appointed as founding members of the Committee:

| Name | Role | Background |
|------|------|------------|
| Mr. Robert Hargreaves | Chair (inaugural) | Former Deputy Secretary, Department of Fair Trading NSW; extensive experience in consumer protection policy and product safety regulation. |
| Dr. Margaret Chen | Member | Senior Lecturer in Materials Engineering, University of Melbourne; specialist in polymer degradation and product failure analysis. |
| Ms. Anita Prasad | Member | Chief Executive, Australian Consumer Advocacy Network; long-standing campaigner for product safety standards for household appliances. |
| Mr. David Okafor | Member | Group Quality Assurance Director, HomeStyle Appliances Pty Ltd; expertise in manufacturing quality systems and supply chain auditing. |
| Ms. Helen T. Wu | Member | Principal Consultant, Standards & Compliance Partners; former manager at Standards Australia, involved in development of AS/NZS electrical safety standards. |
| Mr. James Whitfield | Member | National Secretary, Retailers and Distributors Association of Australia; background in retail logistics and product recall coordination. |
| Prof. Alan R. Stewart | Member | Professor of Consumer Law, University of Sydney; research focus on product liability and consumer redress mechanisms. |
| Ms. Grace Liu | Member | Product Safety Officer, CHOICE (consumer organisation); experience in comparative product testing and public information campaigns. |

**4.3 Appointment of Chair (2021)**

On 1 July 2021, Dr. Margaret Chen was appointed Chair of the Committee, succeeding Mr. Robert Hargreaves whose term concluded on 30 June 2021. Dr. Chen’s appointment as Chair took effect from that date, and she continues to serve in that capacity.

**5. OPERATING ARRANGEMENTS**

**5.1 Meetings**

The Committee shall meet at least four (4) times per calendar year, or more frequently as required by the Minister or the Chair. Meetings may be held in person or by electronic means. The first meeting of the Committee is scheduled for 12 April 2019 at the Department’s offices in Canberra.

**5.2 Quorum**

A quorum of half the current membership, including the Chair (or Deputy Chair if appointed), is required for a meeting to proceed. Decisions are made by consensus where possible; where consensus cannot be reached, matters may be put to a vote, with a simple majority of members present required for a recommendation to be adopted.

**5.3 Subcommittees**

National Consumer Product Quality Committee established_date 2019-03-14 date. Record status: current.

The Committee may establish subcommittees or working groups to consider specific matters, subject to the approval of the Chair. Subcommittees report to the full Committee.

**5.4 Secretariat**

The Department of Industry, Science and Resources provides secretariat support to the Committee. The Secretariat is responsible for arranging meetings, preparing agendas and minutes, and managing correspondence.

**5.5 Reporting**

The Committee reports to the Minister through the Chair. Annual reports and any other formal advice are provided in writing to the Minister.

**6. CONDUCT AND CONFLICT OF INTEREST**

Members are expected to act in the public interest, maintain confidentiality where required, and declare any conflicts of interest at the commencement of each meeting or when a relevant matter arises. Declared conflicts are recorded in the minutes of the meeting.

**7. REVIEW AND TERMINATION**

This Charter will be reviewed within three (3) years of establishment. The Minister may amend the Charter or dissolve the Committee at any time, following consultation with the Chair where practicable.

---

5.1 Working Group on Portable Electric Heaters (WG-2023/04) – Verbal update by Ms. Nguyen (Chair of WG).
Ms. Nguyen reported that the WG had completed its review of test data and incident reports for three models, including the X-1000. A full report was circulated to members prior to the meeting (Attachment 1 – not included in this record). The WG recommended that the Committee consider the safety rating for the X-1000 as a matter of urgency, given the volume of incident reports.

6. NEW BUSINESS – SAFETY RATING OF THE MODEL X-1000 PORTABLE HEATER
[Note: The Chair advised that this item was the subject of a formal motion, to be considered in accordance with the Committee’s procedures for consumer product safety assessments.]

The Model X-1000 Portable Heater has a safety_rating of Unsafe, as decided by the committee. Record status: current.

6.1 Summary of evidence presented:
Ms. Nguyen presented a summary of the test results and incident data for the Model X-1000 Portable Heater (hereafter “the heater”). Key points raised during discussion:
- The heater, manufactured in China and imported by Aussie Home Comforts Pty Ltd, has been on the Australian market since July 2023.
- Testing conducted at an NATA-accredited laboratory (report ref. T-2024-0117) found that the heater’s power cord insulation did not meet the relevant Australian Standard (AS/NZS 60335.2.30) under thermal stress conditions. The test report noted “visible deformation of the cord sheath at temperatures consistent with normal use in a confined space.”
- The heater also failed a drop test, with the rear grille detaching on impact.
- Incident reports: The Committee had before it 14 incident reports received between August 2023 and February 2024, including three reports of minor property damage (scorched carpet, melted cord) and one report of a consumer receiving a mild electric shock (no medical treatment required).
- Mr. Reece, while not formally withdrawing from the discussion, stated that the importer had advised him that they believed the failures were due to “batch-specific issues” and that they had already implemented changes to the production line. He did not provide documentary evidence to the Committee.
- Ms. Nguyen noted that the importer had not yet provided a formal written submission despite being invited to do so on two occasions (letters dated 15 Jan and 5 Feb 2024).
- The Chair noted that the product’s safety_rating of Unsafe is a category rating, as defined in the Committee’s Operating Procedures (Section 4.2). This rating is current and remains in effect until the Committee determines otherwise.
- Dr. Tran (Chair) also noted that a recall recommendation, if passed, would be referred to the ACCC for action.

6.2 Motion:
Moved by Ms. Carla Nguyen: “That the Committee recommends that the Model X-1000 Portable Heater be recalled, and that the safety_rating of the Model X-1000 Portable Heater be recorded as Unsafe, as decided by the committee.”
Seconded by Ms. Fiona Gallagher (Consumer Representative, SA).

6.3 Discussion on the motion:
- Ms. Gallagher noted that the number of incidents, while not high, was significant given the product had only been on the market for eight months. She expressed concern that the heater was sold through major retailers and was likely to be used in bedrooms and other small spaces.
- Mr. Reece asked whether the Committee had considered the importer’s corrective actions. Ms. Nguyen confirmed that the WG had requested evidence of the corrective actions on 12 Feb 2024, but no response had been received as of the meeting date.
- The Chair reminded members that the Committee’s role is to make a recommendation based on available evidence, and that the importer would have the opportunity to make a submission to the ACCC during any recall process.

**Distribution:** The affected heaters were sold nationally through major retailers including Bunnings, Kmart, Target, and The Good Guys, as well as through online marketplaces including Amazon Australia and Catch.com.au. The Model X-1000 Portable Heater has units_affected of 12500, per the recall notice. This figure represents the total number of units imported and supplied to the Australian market within the affected batch range. Record status: current.

**Affected Batch Numbers:** The following batch numbers are affected. The batch number is printed on the base of the heater, adjacent to the compliance label.

The Model X-1000 Portable Heater is fitted with a tip-over switch and a thermal overload protection device. **Supplier's remedy:** Full refund of the purchase price. Proof of purchase is not required.

---

**Recall No. 2024/2056**

**Product:** SafeSwim Pool Fence Latch Kit – Model SFL-200

**Batch / Model Numbers:** All batches manufactured between 1 January 2023 and 30 April 2024 (Batch codes: 2301 through 2404)

**Hazard:** The latch mechanism may fail to fully engage when the gate is closed, allowing the gate to spring open. This presents a drowning hazard for young children. The latch does not comply with the requirements of Australian Standard AS 1926.1 regarding self-latching mechanisms.

**What consumers should do:**

Consumers should immediately check their pool gate to ensure the latch is engaging correctly. If the latch does not click firmly into place, consumers should not rely on the gate for safety and should restrict access to the pool area.

Consumers should contact SafeSwim to receive a free replacement latch kit. Installation instructions will be included. Consumers who are not confident installing the replacement themselves may arrange for a free installation by a licensed tradesperson, with costs covered by SafeSwim.

**Recall No. 2024/2088**

**Product:** KoolBrew Glass Coffee Plunger – 8-Cup Model KB-800

**Batch / Model Numbers:** All units with date codes 2311 through 2405 (printed on the base of the plunger)

**Hazard:** The glass beaker may crack or shatter during normal use due to a manufacturing defect in the glass tempering process. This can cause lacerations and burns from hot liquid. There have been 14 reported incidents in Australia, including 3 injuries requiring medical attention.

**What consumers should do:**

Consumers should immediately stop using the plunger and carefully dispose of the glass beaker. The stainless steel frame and other components can be kept for use with a replacement beaker.

Consumers should contact KoolBrew to receive a free replacement beaker. Proof of purchase is not required. Alternatively, consumers may return the product to the place of purchase for a full refund.

**Hazard:** The mounting bracket may crack and fail when under load, causing the seat to detach from the bicycle. This presents a fall hazard for the child passenger. The product does not comply with the requirements of Australian Standard AS/NZS 4287 for child bike seats.

**What consumers should do:**

Consumers should immediately stop using the bike seat and remove it from the bicycle. Consumers should contact LittleTrekker to receive a free replacement mounting bracket kit. Installation instructions will be included. Consumers who are not confident installing the replacement themselves may arrange for a free installation at an authorised bike shop, with costs covered by LittleTrekker.

**Product:** EcoFresh Laundry Detergent Pods – Lavender Scent – 30-Pack

**Batch / Model Numbers:** All batches with expiry dates between 01/2025 and 06/2025 (Batch codes: 2401A through 2403C)

**Hazard:** The outer film of the pods may burst during transport or handling, releasing concentrated detergent. If the detergent comes into contact with skin or eyes, it can cause irritation and chemical burns. The pods do not comply with the child-resistant packaging requirements of the Poisons Standard.

**What consumers should do:**

Consumers should immediately stop using the pods and keep them out of reach of children. Consumers should contact EcoFresh to receive a full refund. Consumers should not attempt to repackage or transfer the pods to other containers.
